test_title: PYST 27 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 22 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
The sentence below has errors in two parts which are highlighted in bold. Identify the same.

It is impossible to count the number of people **who are given**, (A) and **continue to give**, (B) **their time, efforts, livelihood**, (C) **and lives in the fight** **for** (D) injustice.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in **Part A** lies in the verb tense/voice: "**who are given**." The context describes people who are actively donating or offering their time. Therefore, the active voice "**have given**" should be used to match the parallel active verb "continue to give."
 
• The error in **Part D** lies in the preposition: "**in the fight for injustice**." One does not fight *for* injustice; one fights **against** injustice or **for justice**. In the context of sacrifice (giving lives/livelihood), "against" is the intended meaning.
 
• Parts B and C are grammatically correct within the structure of the list.
 
• Since both A and D contain errors, **Option 4** is the correct choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **AD**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"It is impossible to count the number of people who **have given**, and continue to give, their time, efforts, livelihood, and lives in the fight **against** injustice."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parallelism:** When listing actions (give... and continue to give), the verbs should logically connect to the subject ("people") as the doers of the action. "Are given" makes the people the recipients, which contradicts the rest of the sentence.
 
• **Contextual Prepositions:** Prepositions like *for* and *against* completely change the meaning of the word "fight." Always check the noun following the preposition (injustice) to ensure the sentiment is logical.
